subject.title: Feature request: cron job auto-retry on failure (--retry-count, --retry-delay)

question: Should OpenClaw add per-job cron retry controls on top of the shipped global cron.retry policy, and if so what public CLI/API/storage contract should they use?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow bug fix; it creates durable user-facing retry policy knobs for cron jobs and must settle defaults, side-effect risk, schedule cadence, alert interaction, and compatibility.

options.title: Add additive per-job retry controls
options.body: Define retry fields on cron jobs and wire `cron add`/`cron edit` flags while preserving the current global policy as the default fallback.

options.title: Keep retry policy global only
options.body: Close the per-job flag direction and document that operators should use global `cron.retry` plus failure alerts for now.

options.title: Fold into reason-aware guardrails
options.body: Defer per-job knobs until the broader reason-aware backoff and circuit-breaker design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/14376 is resolved.

recommendation.title: Add additive per-job retry controls
recommendation.body: Define retry fields on cron jobs and wire `cron add`/`cron edit` flags while preserving the current global policy as the default fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the current global recurring retry implementation and is the clearest owner for deciding whether the cron public contract should grow per-job retry fields.
